A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown that the group R is the projection of a larger group T2n on the zero-mode space.
the projective ribbon permutation group, T 2n, governs the statistics (i.e., braiding) of defects of a 3D free-fermions system.
the statistics of the defects in a slowly varying gapped free fermion Hamiltonian is governed by a group T2n which is a quotient of the braid-group on 2n strings.
The main takeaway from our work is that
in a 3D system with a single fermion band and a gapped free- fermion Hamiltonian, there are two types of projective statistics that can occur.
the braiding statistics of non-Abelians in higher dimensions is captured, not in the group of projective transformations, but in the group of ribbon permutations.
the statistics of defects in 3D topological phases are not necessarily Abelian.
